# Implementation review: J-Tech-Japan/intent-system PR #1831 (G842)

You are an independent reviewer on a different runtime from the author. Review pull request #1831 in J-Tech-Japan/intent-system at head e1f2532ea865da26887a7f3d0a1e92f682ff8d7d.

## Inputs

### github-body.md

````github-body.md
# G842: GitHub Copilot CLI and OpenCode as cross-runtime reviewer, conductor, and builder runtimes

## Goal

Make `copilot` (GitHub Copilot CLI) and `opencode` (OpenCode) full members of the cross-runtime review runtime set, beside `codex`, `claude`, and `cursor`. After this unit, any of the five can take any of three roles:

- **Conductor.** Any of the five is a valid `conductor_runtime` in `[[cross_runtime_review.teams]]`.
- **Reviewer.** Any of the five works with `review cross-runtime request`, `record`, and `status`, for both `--kind implementation` and `--kind design`.
- **Builder.** `guide solo-conductor` gives a builder invocation for each of the five, with what each one enforces.

intent-cli still only renders text and records evidence. It never launches a reviewer, a builder, an AI provider CLI, or any process that G842 adds. The one pinned exception is the pre-existing claim-ownership read, which may run `git fetch` through `ClaimOwnershipVerifier` exactly as on the merge base with `main`.

## Why This Slice Exists Now

This is an operator decision of 2026-09-16, marked top priority and to be released (quoted in host `reports/G842-operator-decision-20260916.md`):
- Copilot CLI becomes a design and implementation reviewer (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high effort).
- OpenCode runs local builder sessions, including local models.
- Either may be the `solo-conductor` conductor.
- Every one of the five runtimes may take every role.

Before this unit, the runtime set was closed, so the canonical loop could not carry the operator's chosen reviewer.

## Current Observed State

Before G842 (`ba496314`, v0.32.0-preview.4), the runtime set was `codex`, `claude`, and `cursor` only, verdicts were parsed as one JSON document per file, and no builder lines existed. (`copilot` also names the `guide prompt-matrix` cloud agent and a `skill install` target; neither changes.)

Measured on this Mac on 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17: Copilot CLI 1.0.86-1, OpenCode 1.18.27, claude 2.1.269, and cursor-agent 2026.09.15. The full record, including the AC14 live runs that motivated the 2026-09-17 amendment, is in the host packet's implementation notes, with scrubbed captures in host `reports/G842-runtime-fixtures/`.

## Accepted Baseline You May Assume

- **G834 and G835 rules stay.** The G834/G835 config, stores, gate rules, digest, epoch, publish-flow gate, POSIX quoting, and honest-seat framing are unchanged.
- **Conductor decision (2026-09-17): Copilot model and effort.** The operator's choice of `gpt-5.6-sol` at `high` is this host's seat preference, not a gate policy. The record carries `model` and `effort` so reviewers can check them. A gate-level model and effort policy is a follow-up.
- **No-launch rule.** The `guide model` hard rule "intent-cli must not launch Codex/Claude or any AI provider" holds. Rendered builder and review invocations are text for the seat. Enforcement is by seam tests and a textual guard (AC10), which does not prove the absence of every launch API.
- **Terms.** Confirming each vendor's automation terms is the operator's responsibility.
- **Credentials.** Expired OpenCode `github-copilot` and `openai` tokens are operator state, not a defect.
- **Local models.** The host rule is that a local model provider serves one seat at a time.

## Target Repo / Path / Part

Repository: `J-Tech-Japan/intent-system`

- Target paths: `src/IntentSystem.Cli/`, `tests/IntentSystem.Cli.Tests/`, `docs/en/`, `docs/ja/`

Target part: `copilot and opencode in CrossRuntimeReviewRuntimes (config, request, record, status, gate); pinned read-only invocations, rendered OpenCode reviewer config, JSONL verdict parsing, required --model and optional --effort; an isolated Copilot home in the rendered invocation; guide solo-conductor builder guidance for all five runtimes; en/ja docs and ledger`

## In Scope

- **Runtime names.** `copilot` and `opencode` wherever the runtime set is used.
- **For both new runtimes:** pinned reviewer invocations, allow-lists, and enforcement text; JSONL verdict parsing; embedded implementation prompts; required `--model`; optional `--effort`.
- **Rendered files.** The OpenCode reviewer config, and the isolation directories.
- **Relation.** The relation rule for all five runtimes.
- **Guide.** `guide solo-conductor` builder guidance for all five runtimes.
- **Evidence and docs.** Docs, ledger, tests, and real-run evidence.

## Out Of Scope

- intent-cli launching, supervising, or waiting on any reviewer or builder.
- **Changing codex, claude, or cursor** beyond the runtime-list wording in `Describe()`, the usage lines, and the fix text.
- **Operator directories.** Reading or writing the operator's Copilot home or OpenCode config directories. intent-cli only creates empty isolation directories and reads a given `--opencode-provider-config` file.
- Isolating OpenCode's data, state, or cache directories (credentials live there).
- A trusted-folder or IDE-lock check (the isolated home replaces those sources).
- The unmeasured trust sources listed in section 3.
- Starting or checking a local model server.
- Changing `guide prompt-matrix --agent copilot` or `skill install --target copilot`.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - a vendor or model-family relation (section 6);
  - cursor's argument-form prompt against the Linux argument limit;
  - whether the G834 `cursor-agent --trust` invocation loads workspace MCP servers or hooks;
  - the codex builder line (measure when quota allows);
  - the residual risk of an OpenCode run that exits 0 yet ends at a compaction summary (section 7; never observed);
  - a gate-level Copilot model and effort policy;
  - launch APIs beyond the guard's textual tokens (for example build-time tasks);
  - narrowing the guard's declared-type set to launch-capable types only, since plain DTOs make unrelated units update the table (as G841 had to).

## Standalone Child Issue Contract

**1. Runtime set.**
- **Names.** `CrossRuntimeReviewRuntimes` gains `Copilot = "copilot"` (the GitHub Copilot CLI executable) and `Opencode = "opencode"` (the OpenCode executable). `All` becomes, in order, `codex`, `claude`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `opencode` (ordinal).
- **Wording.** `Describe()` returns `codex, claude, cursor, copilot, or opencode`. `TryRuntime`'s fix text and the usage lines name the same five, and the cause codes are unchanged.
- **Acceptance.** Every `IsSupported` caller (config, both record readers, `request`, `record`, `status`) accepts the two names with no other change.

**2. `--model` and `--effort`.** These rules apply on `request` and `record` for both kinds.
- **`--model` is required for `copilot` and `opencode`.** A missing value refuses `cross-runtime-review-model-required` (new cause), naming the runtime. (Each runtime's default model is user state.) `--model` stays optional for the other three.
- **Existing validation** (G835 `TryValidateModel`) applies to every runtime, plus:
  - **copilot:** `auto`, in any letter case, refuses `cross-runtime-review-model-invalid`, because the model that reviews would be unknown until the run ends.
  - **opencode:** the value must be a provider id, then `/`, then a non-empty remainder. The provider id is `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`. The remainder may contain `/`, spaces, and any non-`Cc` character (for example `local-qwen//Users/me/models/x.gguf`). Anything else refuses `cross-runtime-review-model-invalid`.
  - The value is recorded verbatim (no case folding, no trimming).
- **New optional `--effort <level>`.** The same `TryValidateModel` character rules apply (non-empty, no leading `-`, no `Cc`); a failure refuses `cross-runtime-review-effort-invalid` (new cause).
  - **copilot:** exactly one of `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, rendered as `--reasoning-effort`.
  - **opencode:** any value passing those rules, rendered as `--variant`.
  - **codex, claude, cursor:** `--effort` refuses `cross-runtime-review-argument-invalid`, which names the two runtimes that accept it.
- **`--opencode-provider-config <file>`** (`request` only, `opencode` only, optional). Any other runtime refuses `cross-runtime-review-argument-invalid`.
  - **What the file must be:** UTF-8 JSON whose root object has exactly one key, `provider`, with an object value. Anything else refuses `cross-runtime-review-opencode-provider-config-invalid` (new cause), naming the file and the reason. That includes a missing file, invalid JSON, any other key, or a non-object value.
  - **Why:** built-in providers (`opencode/*`) need no definition. Under isolation, a provider defined only in the global config (such as `omlx070`) needs its block here.
  - **Trust:** the block is operator-authored and copied as-is, including any key. Its `npm` package is installed and loaded by OpenCode.
  - **Result:** the request result names the file as `opencode_provider_config` (`WhenWritingNull`).
- **Rendering.** Both values are always POSIX single-quoted with `ShellQuote`.
- **Record and results.** `record` stores `effort` only when given, next to `model`. The record and request result types declare `effort` with property-level `[JsonIgnore(Condition = WhenWritingNull)]`, because the implementation request result serializes with `Never`. The gate ignores `effort`.

**3. Pinned reviewer invocations.** `invocation.txt` is the existing label line followed by one of these lines. `<ws>` is the workspace, `<out>` is `--out-dir`, and every path, the model, and the effort are `ShellQuote`d. The workspace follows G834/G835: implementation uses `--clone`; design uses `--clone` when given and `--out-dir` otherwise. Bracketed parts appear only when `--effort` is given.

- **copilot:**
  `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL= COPILOT_HOME=<out>/copilot-home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<out>/copilot-xdg copilot -C <ws> --model <model>[ --reasoning-effort <effort>] --available-tools view rg glob --allow-all-tools --disable-builtin-mcps --stream off --output-format json < <out>/prompt.md > <out>/verdict.raw.json`
- **opencode:**
  `rm -f <out>/opencode-exit.txt; OPENCODE_PERMISSION= OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT= XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<out>/opencode-xdg OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=<out>/opencode-config-dir OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1 OPENCODE_CONFIG=<out>/opencode-reviewer.json opencode run --pure --dir <ws> -m <model>[ --variant <effort>] --agent intent-cli-reviewer --format json < <out>/prompt.md > <out>/verdict.raw.json; printf '%s\n' "$?" > <out>/opencode-exit.txt`

**Allow-lists** (`AllowedFlags`):
- **copilot:** `-C`, `--model`, `--reasoning-effort`, `--available-tools`, `--allow-all-tools`, `--disable-builtin-mcps`, `--stream`, `--output-format`.
- **opencode:** `--pure`, `--dir`, `-m`, `--variant`, `--agent`, `--format`.
- **Leading environment assignments** are allowed only as listed:
  - copilot: exactly `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL=`, `COPILOT_HOME=<quoted path>`, and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<quoted path>`, in that order. The two paths are `<out>/copilot-home` and `<out>/copilot-xdg`;
  - opencode: exactly `OPENCODE_PERMISSION=` (empty), `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT=` (empty), `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<quoted path>`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=<quoted path>`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`, and `OPENCODE_CONFIG=<quoted path>`, in that order. The paths are `<out>/opencode-xdg`, `<out>/opencode-config-dir`, and `<out>/opencode-reviewer.json`.
- **Fixed argument positions.**
  - copilot: `--available-tools` is followed by exactly `view`, `rg`, `glob` and then a flag; `--stream` is followed by `off`.
  - opencode: the line starts with exactly `rm -f <out>/opencode-exit.txt;`. This fixed segment is matched whole and excluded from flag checks; `-f` anywhere else is refused. The environment assignments follow it. `run` is the first token after the executable, and `--agent` is followed by `intent-cli-reviewer`. The line ends with exactly `; printf '%s\n' "$?" > <out>/opencode-exit.txt`; measured under bash, sh, and zsh (completed runs wrote `0\n` or `1\n`; a killed process group left no file with the prefix, and left a stale `0\n` without it).
  - Both runtimes: the format flag (`--output-format` for copilot, `--format` for opencode) is followed by `json`.

**Deny list.** The G834 deny list still applies, plus:
- **copilot:** `--allow-all`, `--yolo`, `--allow-all-paths`, `--allow-all-urls`, `--allow-tool`, `--allow-url`, `--add-dir`, `--autopilot`, `--mode`, `--plan`, `--experimental`, `--remote`, `--share`, `--share-gist`, `--enable-all-github-mcp-tools`, `--additional-mcp-config`, `--plugin-dir`, `--agent`, `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL=true`.
- **opencode:** `--auto`, `--attach`, `--share`, `--continue`, `--session`, `--fork`, `--port`, `--command`, `--interactive`, `-i`, a non-empty `OPENCODE_PERMISSION` or `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and `XDG_DATA_HOME`.

**`ReadOnlyEnforcement`.** These statements are rendered into the request result and summarized in the guide:
- **copilot:**
  - `--available-tools view rg glob` leaves only those three tools, so the reviewer reads files but cannot write or run commands. Path verification refuses reads outside the workspace.
  - `--disable-builtin-mcps` disables the GitHub MCP server. With the isolated home, the operator's user MCP servers do not start (measured). Any other MCP server's tools would not be exposed anyway.
  - `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL=` stops the environment variable from trusting the workspace. `COPILOT_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` point at empty directories that intent-cli created under the out-dir, so the operator's `trustedFolders`, IDE lock files, user hooks, and user MCP servers are not read.
  - **Credentials.** With the isolated home, Copilot runs `gh auth token --hostname github.com` itself (measured), so a signed-in real `gh` must be first on PATH. intent-cli never launches it.
  - Unmeasured trust sources (see the implementation notes) are mitigated by the isolated home and by using no SDK or ACP host.
- **opencode:**
  - The rendered config denies every tool (`*`) and allows only read, glob, grep, and list, at the top level and for the `intent-cli-reviewer` agent.
  - `task` is denied because agent-level denials do not reach subagents: a reviewer delegated a file change to the `general` subagent.
  - `external_directory` is denied, so reads outside the workspace are refused.
  - `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1` and `--pure` stop the workspace's config, agents, plugins, and MCP entries from overriding these rules or running code, and its `AGENTS.md` does not reach the model (measured with a canary).
  - The isolated config directories and the two empty variables keep out the operator's global config and any inherited overrides. Each re-enabled writes when not isolated, and the full form held against all of them (measured).
  - Data, state, and cache stay the operator's (credentials); they were not probed as permission sources.

**3a. Isolation directories and safe writes.**
- **Creation.** `request` (both kinds) creates empty `<out>/copilot-home` and `<out>/copilot-xdg` for copilot, and empty `<out>/opencode-xdg` and `<out>/opencode-config-dir` for opencode, and lists them in `files` after the rendered files.
- **Existing run outputs.** An existing `opencode-exit.txt` or `verdict.raw.json` in the out-dir is refused as a foreign entry (`out-dir-not-empty`, as measured at `ccd06fff`); `request` never deletes one.
- **Existing directories.** An empty one is accepted. A file with that name, or a non-empty directory, refuses the existing `out-dir-not-empty`, so each run needs a new out-dir.
- **Reads.** intent-cli never reads or writes the operator's homes, and reads nothing inside the isolation directories (the runtimes write there).
- **Protected homes.** `$HOME/.copilot`, `COPILOT_HOME`, `$HOME/.config/opencode`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `$HOME/.local/share/opencode`, and `XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode`.
- **Before writing,** `request` refuses `cross-runtime-review-path-invalid` in either of these cases:
  - **A planned path overlaps a protected home.** Planned paths are the out-dir, every planned isolation directory, and every rendered file. Each planned path and each existing home is resolved (existing prefix, symlinks followed) and compared case-insensitively. A planned path that equals, is inside, or contains a protected home is refused. Examples:
    - `~/.config/opencode -> ~/dotfiles/opencode` with `--out-dir ~/dotfiles/opencode/r1`;
    - `COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/review/copilot-home` with `--out-dir /tmp/review`.
  - **An existing planned path is not safe.** An existing rendered path or isolation directory is a symlink (dangling included), resolves outside the resolved out-dir, or, for a rendered file, is not a regular file.
- **Replace-write.** Each rendered file is written to a new temporary file in the out-dir and atomically renamed over the target, never truncated in place. An existing hard link to an outside file is therefore left untouched.
- **Measured at `ccd06fff`** (implementation notes): each case above was accepted, and a hard-linked `prompt.md` had its outside file overwritten in place.
- **No trusted-folder check** is performed; the isolation directories are created empty.

**4. Rendered files.**
- **Per-runtime file set.** `CrossRuntimeReviewFiles` gains `OpencodeReviewerConfig = "opencode-reviewer.json"` and a per-runtime set `RenderedFor(runtime)`:
  - the three existing files for codex, claude, and cursor;
  - the same three plus the empty directories `copilot-home` and `copilot-xdg` for copilot;
  - the same three plus `opencode-reviewer.json` and the empty directories `opencode-xdg` and `opencode-config-dir` for opencode. The run later adds `verdict.raw.json`, and for opencode also `opencode-exit.txt`.
  The out-dir foreign-entry check and `files` use `RenderedFor(runtime)`, so other runtimes' leftovers are foreign, and codex, claude, and cursor results are unchanged.
- **The OpenCode config file.** `opencode-reviewer.json` is written as UTF-8 without a BOM, byte-for-byte equal to the fixture `Fixtures/G842/opencode-reviewer.measured.json`:
  - Each permission object has `"*": "deny"` first.
  - Then these keys are each `"deny"`, in this order: `edit`, `bash`, `task`, `external_directory`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `skill`, `todowrite`, `question`, `lsp`, `doom_loop`.
  - Then these keys are each `"allow"`, in this order: `read`, `glob`, `grep`, `list`.
  - The same object appears as top-level `permission` and as `agent.intent-cli-reviewer.permission`, with `"mode": "primary"` and a fixed description.
  - Because opencode applies the last matching rule, the order is part of the contract.
  - **With `--opencode-provider-config`:** a `"provider"` member holding the file's `provider` value is inserted right after `$schema`. It uses the same 2-space indentation and keeps its key order. For `opencode-provider-omlx070.input.json`, the result equals `opencode-reviewer-with-provider.rendered.json` byte-for-byte (the file used in the measured runs).

**5. Prompts.**
- **Implementation review, copilot and opencode.** Both runtimes refuse reads outside the workspace (measured), so the implementation prompt embeds `github-body.md`, `review-context.md`, and `implementation.md` verbatim instead of listing their host paths. It uses the existing `AppendEmbeddedFile` framing, in that order. Everything else is the same as `RenderPrompt`: repo, PR, head, clone path, rules, output section, and schema.
- **Other cases.** The codex, claude, and cursor implementation prompts are byte-identical to the branch's merge base with `main`. The design prompt is unchanged for all five runtimes.
- **Invalid UTF-8.** A packet file that is not valid UTF-8 refuses `cross-runtime-review-packet-invalid`, as in design review.

**6. Relation rule** (one rule for all five runtimes, unchanged in form).
- `relation` is `same-runtime` exactly when the reviewer's `--runtime` equals the declared `conductor_runtime` (ordinal), and `cross-runtime` otherwise.
- The rule is by CLI runtime, not by model vendor or provider.

| conductor ↓ / reviewer → | codex | claude | cursor | copilot | opencode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| codex | same | cross | cross | cross | cross |
| claude | cross | same | cross | cross | cross |
| cursor | cross | cross | same | cross | cross |
| copilot | cross | cross | cross | same | cross |
| opencode | cross | cross | cross | cross | same |

So `opencode` running `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol` is `cross-runtime` for a `copilot` or `codex` conductor. A declared team needs a same-runtime approve and a cross-runtime approve on the key, exactly as in G834/G835.

**Why:** the declared runtime is the only verifiable fact (see the implementation notes). The guide advises a reviewer model of a different vendor and family than the conductor's; the gate does not check this.

**7. Verdict envelopes.** `TryParse` and `TryParseDesign` gain the two runtimes and report the observed model for copilot.

- **Common JSONL rules** (both runtimes):
  - The file is UTF-8 and is split on `\n`. A single trailing empty segment is ignored.
  - Every other segment must be one JSON object with a string `type`; otherwise `verdict-invalid` names the 1-based line number.
  - An empty file is refused.
  - A file whose first line is a JSON object with `verdict` and no `type` is refused as a bare verdict ("requires the runtime JSON envelope from the pinned invocation"), as for claude and cursor.
  - Unknown event types are ignored.
- **Verdict text** (copilot and opencode). Lines are taken after trimming trailing whitespace, and a *fence line* is one that starts, after optional spaces, with three backticks.
  - **Fenced form.** If the last line is exactly three backticks, the text must contain exactly two fence lines. The opener must be exactly three backticks, or three backticks followed by `json`. The lines between them must parse as exactly one JSON object and nothing else. Narration before the opener is accepted.
  - **Unfenced form.** Otherwise, any fence line in the text refuses (this covers text after a closing fence and an unterminated fence). The verdict is taken by the existing `TryParseTrailingObject`: narration before the object is accepted, nothing after it is.
  - **Refusals.** Every other case is refused as `verdict-invalid`, naming the rule: more than one fenced block, another opener, invalid JSON in the fence, or a fence holding anything besides one object.
  - **Validation.** The object is then validated by the existing `TryValidate` or `TryValidateDesign`.
  - **Cursor is unchanged.** It keeps its existing fence refusal cause and message byte-for-byte, as on the branch's merge base with `main`. A fenced cursor verdict was first measured as refused on `ba496314`, because the text must end with `}`.
- **copilot:**
  1. The last event is the only `type: "result"` event, and its `exitCode` is the integer `0`.
  2. Exactly one event is `type: "assistant.message"` with `data.phase == "final_answer"`.
  3. That event has a string `data.content`, and its `data.toolRequests` is absent or an empty array.
  4. Its `data.model` is a string, returned as the observed model.
  5. When `--effort` is given, the observed effort is checked. It is taken from every `session.usage_checkpoint` event: in `data.promptCacheBreakState`, the entries with `conversation == "main"`, then `models[<observed model>].reasoning_effort`.

  The events are checked in that order. A failure of 1, 2, or 3 is `verdict-invalid`, naming which rule failed. A failure of 4, or an observed model that differs from `--model` (ordinal), refuses `cross-runtime-review-model-mismatch` (new cause), naming both values. For rule 5, the command refuses `cross-runtime-review-effort-mismatch` (new cause) when there is no such value, or when any value differs from `--effort` (ordinal). I chose a separate cause rather than `model-mismatch` because the fix is different. Every captured copilot envelope carries this value, and it matches the flag used. Without `--effort`, nothing is checked and no effort is recorded.
- **opencode:**
  The events are read in order through this transition table, starting in `idle`. Rows are checked top to bottom, and every refusal is `verdict-invalid`, naming the row and the 1-based line. A **reopen event** is a `text` event whose `part.type == "text"`, `part.synthetic` is the boolean `true`, and `part.metadata.compaction_continue` is the boolean `true`.

  | row | state | event | result |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | T1 | any | `error` | refuse, with `error.name` and `error.data.message` |
  | T2 | `terminated` | a reopen event | go to `idle` (compaction); its text is never part of the answer |
  | T3 | `terminated` | any other event | refuse |
  | T4 | `idle`, `open` | `text` with `part.synthetic == true` | refuse |
  | T5 | `idle` | `step_start` | go to `open`, with an empty text buffer |
  | T6 | `idle` | `step_finish`, `text`, `tool_use` | refuse |
  | T7 | `open` | `step_start` | refuse |
  | T8 | `open` | `step_finish` with `part.reason == "stop"` | go to `terminated` |
  | T9 | `open` | `step_finish` with any other reason | go to `idle` |
  | T10 | `open` | `text` | stay; append `part.text` |
  | T11 | `open` | `tool_use` | stay |
  | T12 | `idle`, `open` | any other type | ignore |
  | T13 | end of file | state is not `terminated`, or the last buffer is empty | refuse |

  **Answer.** The answer is the last step before the final terminal `stop`. A capture that exits 0 yet ends at a compaction summary `stop` is an accepted, unobserved residual (below).

  **Accepted residual risk** (non-blocking): no field marks a summary step (measured). Killed or truncated runs fail the exit check (section 8). A run that exits 0 but ends at a summary `stop` was never observed, and would still need a matching digest or head SHA and a verdict object.

  All real captures behave as the implementation notes record. OpenCode events carry no model id or effort, so opencode's recorded `model` and `effort` are seat-reported and unchecked (stated in the guide and docs).

**8. Record and comment.** Recording is unchanged except as follows:
- The runtime set, model, and effort rules above apply.
- The comment body names `effort` when present, after `model`.
- For both kinds, the record writes succeed with the new runtimes and can be read back.
- **OpenCode exit status.** `record --runtime opencode` requires a regular file `opencode-exit.txt` (not a symlink) in the verdict file's directory.
  - If it is absent, the command refuses `cross-runtime-review-exit-status-missing` (new cause).
  - If its bytes are anything other than exactly `0\n`, it refuses `cross-runtime-review-exit-status-nonzero` (new cause), showing the content.
  - A killed run is refused: SIGTERM mid-compaction wrote `143\n` (measured). Copilot's `result` event already carries `exitCode`.
- Records of the three existing runtimes are byte-identical to the branch's merge base with `main` when `--effort` is absent.

**9. `guide solo-conductor`.**
- **Steps 3 and 7.** The runtime placeholders become `<codex|claude|cursor|copilot|opencode>`. Step 7 adds:
  - one sentence per new runtime from section 3;
  - that copilot and opencode reviewers may return the verdict as one trailing fenced JSON object;
  - that `--model` is required for copilot and opencode;
  - the vendor and model-family advice from section 6, including that the gate does not check it.
- **New `builder` field** in the JSON and a "Builder invocations (guidance)" Markdown section after the loop. Step 6's instruction points to it. The field holds:
  - `contract`, which states each of its seven items once:
    1. The conductor runs one builder at a time in the unit's isolated clone (step 6), outside every runtime's trusted folders. The copilot builder line uses a fresh, empty `COPILOT_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` per run (for example from `mktemp -d`, removed afterwards). ### Why the relation stays by runtime (full)

**Why the relation stays by runtime:**
- **The same-runtime slot is a runtime property.** It stands for the independent reviewer started in the conductor's own runtime.
- **The declared runtime is the only verifiable fact.** Neither the conductor's model nor its vendor is declared.
- **Vendor cannot be derived reliably from model ids.**
  - cursor already hosts Claude, GPT, and Grok models (G835 recorded `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh` with a Claude conductor).
  - Copilot and OpenCode's `github-copilot` provider host several vendors.
  - `opencode/*` ids name no vendor, and local ids are file paths.
- **Records already show the model.** G834's "independent perspectives" intent is served by a different CLI, tool harness, system prompt, and session, and each record and comment names the model.
- **The guide carries vendor advice.** The guide tells the seat to choose a cross-runtime reviewer model from a vendor other than the conductor's model. The seat should also pick a model family different from the conductor's model. For example, an opencode conductor on `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol` and a copilot reviewer on `gpt-5.6-sol` are still `cross-runtime`, and the gate does not check this. A declared vendor dimension is out of scope and recorded as a follow-up (conductor ruling, 2026-09-16).

  | T2 | `terminated` | a reopen event | go to `idle` (compaction); its text is never part of the answer |
  | T3 | `terminated` | any other event | refuse |
  | T4 | `idle`, `open` | `text` with `part.synthetic == true` | refuse |
  | T5 | `idle` | `step_start` | go to `open`, with an empty text buffer |
  | T6 | `idle` | `step_finish`, `text`, `tool_use` | refuse |
  | T7 | `open` | `step_start` | refuse |
  | T8 | `open` | `step_finish` with `part.reason == "stop"` | go to `terminated` |
  | T9 | `open` | `step_finish` with any other reason | go to `idle` |
  | T10 | `open` | `text` | stay; append `part.text` |
  | T11 | `open` | `tool_use` | stay |
  | T12 | `idle`, `open` | any other type | ignore |
  | T13 | end of file | state is not `terminated`, or the last buffer is empty | refuse |

  **Answer.** The answer is the last step before the final terminal `stop`. A capture that exits 0 yet ends at a compaction summary `stop` is an accepted, unobserved residual (below).

  **Accepted residual risk** (non-blocking): no field marks a summary step (measured). Killed or truncated runs fail the exit check (section 8). A run that exits 0 but ends at a summary `stop` was never observed, and would still need a matching digest or head SHA and a verdict object.

  All real captures behave as the implementation notes record. OpenCode events carry no model id or effort, so opencode's recorded `model` and `effort` are seat-reported and unchecked (stated in the guide and docs).

### Why the relation stays by runtime (full)

**Why the relation stays by runtime:**
- **The same-runtime slot is a runtime property.** It stands for the independent reviewer started in the conductor's own runtime.
- **The declared runtime is the only verifiable fact.** Neither the conductor's model nor its vendor is declared.
- **Vendor cannot be derived reliably from model ids.**
  - cursor already hosts Claude, GPT, and Grok models (G835 recorded `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh` with a Claude conductor).
  - Copilot and OpenCode's `github-copilot` provider host several vendors.
  - `opencode/*` ids name no vendor, and local ids are file paths.
- **Records already show the model.** G834's "independent perspectives" intent is served by a different CLI, tool harness, system prompt, and session, and each record and comment names the model.
- **The guide carries vendor advice.** The guide tells the seat to choose a cross-runtime reviewer model from a vendor other than the conductor's model. The seat should also pick a model family different from the conductor's model. For example, an opencode conductor on `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol` and a copilot reviewer on `gpt-5.6-sol` are still `cross-runtime`, and the gate does not check this. A declared vendor dimension is out of scope and recorded as a follow-up (conductor ruling, 2026-09-16).
